version_policy: Each global candidate proposes 2.0.1 directly from inspected actual2.0.0; includes prior uninstalled observability additions and new conformance additions. Previous proposal files remain historical. Project drafts apply accumulated0.2 additions plus0.3 conformance in owning repository only.

files.addition:
## Input evidence and observed algorithm changes
Before dependent work, use the current packet's effective prerequisites and check
that the required output is available in the relevant workspace. Free status text
or a collapsed parent arrow alone is insufficient. If an edge is inaccurate,
revise its bounded contract or record an explained deviation; preserve actual
work and unknown evidence. The observer is not an execution authority.

At meaningful changes to a registered custom algorithm, update exact implementation
and affected test/measurement references. Separate authored tests, executed evidence,
correctness and resource claims. A changed implementation can make evidence stale;
it does not make an old run fail. Do not declare an optimization measured without
compatible data/method evidence. Do not maintain a second Plan status document or
ask the model to summarize streams merely to refresh the UI. These rules preserve
optional chat supply and the already selected resource permissions.

## Waypoint execution trace and completion evidence
When Waypoint observation is in scope, follow the owning project's workflow contract.
Before implementation, validate this executor's own native binding and declare the
packet scope. Each child does this with its own identity; never copy a parent's
binding or rely on a shared session ID. A missing binding leaves native messages
unassigned; resolve it once without inventing attribution or blocking unrelated
permitted work. Scope is observational, not an exclusive claim or agent control.

At meaningful check boundaries record the actual outcome against existing criterion
IDs with run ID, immutable evidence reference and applicable revision/environment.
Register executed checks before reporting the packet complete. Reused evidence
retains its original run basis; retrospective registration says it is retrospective,
without an invented past timestamp. Distinguish skipped/not_run, failed/error and
unverified claims. A manual --current declaration is not automatic verification of
current code. Empty chat proves neither success nor failure. Never add synthetic
notes, guessed historical links or repeated tests just to fill the map.

Before done, compare the packet's expected result and criteria with the observed
result. Record exceptions, missing checks and the smallest remaining fix explicitly;
partial delivery may be described honestly without calling it accepted. Completion
records do not close focus automatically: release or redeclare this executor's scope
at handoff. Preserve original events and IDs. No heartbeat, extra model polling,
permission gate, global installation or start/resume/stop command is introduced.

## Human-readable plans and evidenced dependencies
For each meaningful node, author its project context, intended change and observable
outcome separately from the executor assignment. The owner's Plan outline and Task
view use the same intent; join status from existing node events, never ask an agent
to maintain a second status summary. Preserve legacy technical assignments.

A hard edge names a required producer output, affected consumer scope, start/finish
phase and evidence of availability. Keep preferred coding order and containment
separate. Check inherited dependencies using the SAME resolver in packet/frontier
and UI projections; collapsed links disclose their actual endpoints. Do not infer
input availability from free status text alone. The observer preserves early work
and unknown evidence instead of enforcing an execution gate.

Use the project's compatible machine-readable profile as the common authoring
source, preserving IDs, version guards and unknown extensions. Add algorithm
references only for substantial custom logic needing correctness/cost review;
framework names and trivial wrappers are not inventory entries. Runtime algorithm
checks/measurements remain evidence, not repeated plan editing.

Chat capsules remain OPTIONAL supply for a node's result. Every roadmap retains a
permitted non-chat route; absence of chat delivery is not a hard dependency. Existing
claims and integration ownership still prevent duplicate work. These additions do
not change the selected resource policy, create schedules or authorize installation.

## Scenario evidence and completion meaning
For every meaningful packet map acceptance IDs to concrete user scenarios and the
least costly evidence that establishes each claim. Distinguish source inspection,
unit/contract checks, synthetic browser-to-HTTP integration, actual installed service
and actual native-source integration. Include relevant negative cases: unavailable
or stale input, failure, empty history, late receipt, reconnect and incompatible
revision where applicable; do not demand every case for unrelated simple work.

Specify output identity/revision, applicable workspace and start/finish phase for a
real required input; preferred order stays an order edge. Plan availability evidence
separately from done status. Stable immutable evidence references must survive later
validation rather than being overwritten under the same historical filename. State
what invalidates reused evidence and what remains unverified. Do not create fake
execution history, authored passing tests or runtime summaries in the plan.

The handoff must tell each permitted executor to use its own binding, declare scope
before work, record actual checks by criterion ID before completion, and release scope
at handoff. Use one graph, readable intent and a separate technical assignment. A
completed count alone cannot claim all scenarios or an entire product passed. Keep
real unresolved work explicit; fix packets link the original issue and preserve valid
unaffected work. This adds no approval gate, mandatory repeated audit or agent control.

## Waypoint map-to-evidence conformance
At the requested boundary compare the accepted graph/version with its status,
criterion receipts, scope declarations and actual executed scenario evidence. Check
binding coverage for each executor, declaration-before-work and release-at-handoff;
empty chats, an active declared scope and done are distinct observations. Preserve
native attribution. Do not guess missing historical links or infer physical absence
only because an availability receipt arrived late.

For each claim state expected behavior, observed behavior, evidence level, run/capture
basis, affected revision/workspace, consequence and concrete cause or uncertainty.
Verify referenced artifact identity where available. A mutable file at a historical
path or a writer-supplied current label does not prove fresh current-code validation.
Treat retrospective criterion registration explicitly; 47 green receipts cannot by
themselves prove all product scenarios passed. Separate old failed attempts, actual
repairs, synthetic reproductions and real-source integration.

Reopen or route a linked -FIX when an accepted requirement is demonstrably missing,
a required claimed check was not run, evidence materially contradicts completion or
a current required artifact is unavailable. Use an unverified finding when evidence
is insufficient, not a fabricated failure; optional improvements stay optional.
Preserve valid passes, original receipts and unexplained historical gaps. Plan the
smallest targeted proof for the repair; do not rerun every suite or rewrite the plan
just to remove a warning. No new execution gate or publication permission follows.
